howToRegenerate: node scripts/check-content.mjs --print-baseline  (prints this shape; it never writes it)
ruleOfExit: A pair leaves this file when the copy is deleted or a ruling settles it. It is NOT kept with status 'resolved': a signature in this file is an exemption, so keeping a closed pair would let the same duplicate ship again without going red. The pairs closed by S018/D262 and by D273 are listed in `resolved` below for provenance only.
signatureNote: A signature has its date stamps removed before anything else (DATE_STAMP in scripts/check-content.mjs). `npm run events:harvest` rewrites "Copied from the club's own calendar on <date>" each time the feed is read, and a signature that carries the stamp's date is an exemption with an expiry: @measured 2026-11-13 by this gate, one harvest moved the stamp from Nov 6 to Nov 13 and made all 3 baseline rows stale — three FAILs for sentences nobody edited. The date the page prints is data, not the shape of the sentence. Since D322 the same line reads "yesterday" or "11 days ago" inside the 30-day window, so the relative ages are stripped too: a signature that matches only a calendar date expires every time anybody runs the build. @measured 2026-11-14 by `node scripts/check-content.mjs --print-baseline`, which prints exactly one live pair against the five emitted pages. A signature is also NOT derived from a section heading: on 2026-11-13 a row's `surfaces` prose named a heading that was the harvester's copy of the organizer's title, and the heading had to be corrected (D301) while the signature stayed valid.

scores: content words only; sentences split on terminal punctuation only. A pair is a pair when it shares >=3 content words and (Jaccard >= 0.45 or overlap >= 0.5). Overlap is shared words over the SHORTER sentence, because a paraphrase of a long sentence scores low on Jaccard alone.

statusMeaning.open: the repeat is real and unruled: the gate stays green on it; deleting one side or taking a ruling is the exit
statusMeaning.deliberate: the repeat is the point of the surface - a source line or a ruling says so, in why
statusMeaning.template: identical row furniture on sibling rows: one string rendered twice. Coupling, not duplication - if one row changes, both must

rowFurniture.what: Strings printed in more than one schedule row (`<li data-surface="row">`). The gate computes them from the artifact every run and reports them; it never reads this list, so this is provenance, not an exemption. A row and a section paragraph printing the same sentence still FAILS, and two rows that paraphrase each other still FAILS - the exemption is only for the identical string in two rows (proven by `check:content:selftest`, plants `row-furniture-not-a-duplicate`, `row-sentence-in-a-section-paragraph`, `rows-that-paraphrase`).
rowFurniture.ruledBy: D273 (row furniture is coupling, not duplication)

pairs.why: The same provenance rule on the schedule page: the page lede and the list stamp each say where the dates came from. D218 keeps the stamp once for the list rather than once per row. The stamp now reads 'yesterday' rather than a date, because D322 makes a provenance line say how long ago inside 30 days and when beyond it - the signature survives that change because DATE_STAMP strips relative ages too. Corrected 2026-11-13: this row's `surfaces` used to read `section:Matheapolis - Bimonthly Social`, because it was measured against rows whose page title was the harvester's copy of the organizer's SUMMARY. The title is D189's ruled name again (`MPLS Math Club Social`) and the cadence word lives only in the feed (D301), so the heading this stamp inherits no longer contains one. The signature is unchanged - it was never derived from the heading - and `check:content` now fails any page that prints a cadence word its source does not name.
